title: Rooftop Ranger
summary: Stun runaway robots from a rooftop at night by tilting a scope that only swings through the principal branch of tan⁻¹, sin⁻¹ or cos⁻¹.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Pythagoras for the line of sight
learningOutcome: The student can turn a height, distance or offset into an exact angle with tan⁻¹, sin⁻¹ or cos⁻¹, keep it inside the principal branch with the right sign, and find a line of sight by Pythagoras.

levels.title: Down the street
levels.adds: Baseline: the tilt is tan⁻¹(−height/distance) in (−π/2, π/2), with the special ratios 1/√3, 1 and √3 (Ex 2.1 Q4, Q6, Q8).
hints: Looking down is a negative tilt.
tan of the tilt = −(roof height)/(street distance). Cancel the common factor first.

levels.title: Range turret
levels.adds: New: the range turret needs the straight-line distance, found by Pythagoras from the height and the street distance, as well as the tilt.
hints: The line of sight is the hypotenuse of the triangle formed by the building and the street.
Set the tilt first, then the range: a miss tells you which of the two drifted.

levels.title: Drones and ledges
levels.adds: New: targets above and below, so the tilt is sin⁻¹(height/range) with its sign, inside [−π/2, π/2] (Ex 2.1 Q1, Q13).
hints: Above the scope is positive, below is negative.
sin of the tilt = (signed height)/(laser range).
sin⁻¹(−x) = −sin⁻¹(x), and sin⁻¹(1) = π/2 points straight up.

levels.title: The wall turret
levels.adds: New: a turret on a wall swings through [0, π], the branch of cos⁻¹, so a robot to the west needs an obtuse bearing (Ex 2.1 Q2, Q5, Q9).
hints: cos of the bearing = (east offset)/(range); a west offset is negative.
The turret cannot point behind the wall, so the answer is never negative.

misconceptions: An angle of depression is a positive tilt
